title: multilingual-classics-markdown corpus manifest
description: Schema for manifest.json, the machine-readable index of every book in the corpus. The manifest is generated by scripts/build-manifest.py and its per-book fields mirror each book's YAML frontmatter, which is specified in FRONTMATTER.md. Frontmatter keys are reproduced verbatim; the manifest adds path, locale and the three derived numeric fields.

bookCount.description: Number of entries in books. Cross-checked against the corpus tree by build-manifest.py --check and against the prose counts in README, CORPUS and CITATION by check-doc-counts.py.

locales.description: Every BCP-47 locale directory under books/, sorted.

books.description: One entry per book, sorted by path.

bcp47.description: BCP-47 language tag, carrying region and script subtags where they matter (es-MX, zh-Hans, pt-BR). Directory names under books/ are these tags.

book.description: One book. The required set is the provenance layer from FRONTMATTER.md plus the fields build-manifest.py derives.

path.description: Repo-relative path, books/<locale>/<author>/<title>.md. This is the identity of a book; manifest.json keys on it. See the README section on pinning for the rename protocol.

locale.description: The locale directory the book sits in. Equal to language in every current entry, and kept separate because the directory is the addressing key.

title.description: The work's title, in its own language and orthography.

author.description: The author, in their own language where the source gives it. May carry combined attribution for collected oral literature.

language.description: BCP-47 tag for the text itself.

year.description: Publication year of the cited source edition, as a string. Approximate, era-qualified and serial-range forms are permitted: 1915, c. 1280, c. 399 BCE, 1887-1906.

yearNumeric.description: year reduced to a sortable integer, negative for BCE. The upper bound is the corpus's public-domain cutoff: the year field records the source edition, and no source edition in the corpus postdates 1928. Books whose transmission base is a later edition record that in year_note or source_note, not here.

source.description: The upstream repository or archive name. See CORPUS.md, Provenance.

source_url.description: Direct URL to the source that was fetched.

license.const: Public domain in the United States
license.description: Constant across the corpus. Where a book's public-domain basis is not simple pre-1929 publication, the basis is stated in source_note rather than varied here.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the markdown file on disk, frontmatter included.

wordCount.description: Whitespace-delimited word count of the body. Not meaningful for the scriptio continua languages (ja, zh, th), where it approximates line or character runs instead.

year_note.description: First publication against transcription-base edition, serial publication, manuscript dating. Where the transmission base postdates 1928, this field or source_note says so.

source_note.description: Source caveats: OCR noise tier, named corrections, retrieval route, attribution uncertainty, and the public-domain basis where it is not simple pre-1929 publication.

selection_note.description: Required whenever the file is an excerpt. Explains what is included, what is omitted, and why.

language_note.description: Rationale where the BCP-47 tag choice needs defending.

edition_note.description: Notes on the specific printing where edition choice is itself the interesting fact.

translator.description: Only where a translation is included. The translation must itself be pre-1929.

title_translit.description: Standard romanization of the title. ASCII-friendly, not scholarly diacritic transliteration.

title_en.description: The work's established English title, or a plain gloss where none exists. A finding aid rather than a fresh translation.

text_quality.description: Present only on books known to fall short of the corpus's normal fidelity bar, so consumers can filter them out. noisy: machine OCR or otherwise unproofread, disclosed residual character noise, readable and structurally sound. alpha: known substantial problems, provisional, treat as a placeholder. Absent by default. Every book carrying this field has a matching open flag in QUALITY.md.

writing-mode.description: The work's conventional writing direction, in the CSS writing-mode value space. Absence means horizontal.
